em.why: no pinned source states CR0.EM of the declared machine (ks386.inc CR0_EM is a bit constant only; Wine runs on the host CPU); user mode observes CR0 only through smsw, which is itself undecided; blocker: a reach certificate that no site depends on it, or an owner decision to derive it from the CPUID record

mp.why: no pinned source states CR0.MP (ks386.inc CR0_MP is a bit constant only); user mode sees it only through smsw (undecided)

ts.why: no pinned source; user mode sees TS only through smsw (undecided); Windows handles #NM transparently (lazy FPU switch), and the lazy-switch behaviour is not a pinned source

pce.why: rdpmc at CPL 3 needs CR4.PCE = 1; the SDM only defines the bit, the declared CPU's cpuid does not state it, the WDK 7.1 constants name no PCE bit and Wine 9.0 has no rdpmc case

tsd.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: is_privileged_instr intercepts only the 0F opcodes ['0x20', '0x21', '0x22', '0x23'], so rdtsc (0F 31) runs in user mode; consistent with the owner's decision that rdtsc reads the platform timer

umip.source: Intel SDM Vol 3A 2.5 CR4.UMIP: the bit is reserved (setting it is #GP) unless CPUID.(EAX=07H,ECX=0):ECX[2] is enumerated; the declared CPU's max basic leaf is 4 (ports/fnv-nx/verify/cpuid_model.json max_basic @ a3217cd2c604), below 7, so there is no leaf 7 and CR4.UMIP is 0

osfxsr.why: no pinned source states CR4.OSFXSR (ks386.inc CR4_FXSR = 0x200 is a bit constant only); the declared CPU's cpuid (verify/cpuid_model.json leaf 1 EDX) advertises FXSR/SSE/SSE2, but whether the OS enabled them is not a pinned fact; blocker: an owner/L3b decision to take OS support from the CPUID record, or a reach certificate

osxmmexcpt.why: no pinned source states CR4.OSXMMEXCPT (ks386.inc CR4_XMMEXCPT = 0x400 is a bit constant only); with the initial MXCSR 0x1F80 every SIMD exception is masked, so #XM is not raised until a site unmasks it; blocker: a certificate that every ldmxcsr / fxrstor site keeps the exceptions masked (CLAUDE.md fact, not yet certified)

initial.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: the initial thread context, context.EFlags

iopl.source: bits 12-13 of the initial EFLAGS (Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6)

iopl_user_modifiable.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): EFLAGS_USER_SANITIZE = 0x3F4DD7, the EFLAGS bits user code can set; bits 12-13 are not in it

idtr_limit.why: the number of gates of the OS's IDT is not stated by a pinned source (the SDM allows 256 entries at most)

41.why: MSDN __fastfail intrinsic: fast fail is supported from Windows 8 (build 9200); Windows 7 SP1 is build 7601, so int 0x29 is not a fast-fail gate there. What the instruction does on build 7601 is not stated by MSDN: undecided

other_vectors.source: Intel SDM Vol 2 INT n and Vol 3 6.12.1.1 (a user-mode int n at a vector whose gate is not DPL 3 is #GP with error code n*8+2, IDT bit set, EXT 0, saved EIP = the int instruction); Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: segv_handler TRAP_x86_PROTFLT lines 1925-1941 (err != 0 skips is_privileged_instr; (err & 7) == 2 calls handle_interrupt, which returns FALSE at its `default` line 1804 for every vector but 0x29 and 0x2d; then EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, NumberParameters 2, ExceptionInformation[0] = 0, [1] = 0xffffffff, check_invalid_gs (line 1279) returns FALSE for opcode 0xCD); setup_exception_record line 1449: ExceptionAddress = EIP_sig, context Eip not advanced; segv_handler line 1905: rec = { 0 } so ExceptionFlags 0 (continuable). Precedence (2): MSDN and the WDK state nothing for these vectors; vector 0x29 stays in `excluded`

int_ring3.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: handle_interrupt cases ['0x2d']; segv_handler / trap_handler map ['TRAP_x86_BPTFLT', 'TRAP_x86_OFLOW'] to #OF / #BP

es.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3

fs.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3

gs.source: KGDT_R3_DATA and KGDT_R3_TEB are the ring-3 data segments of the WDK's GDT constants (ks386.inc); SDM Vol 3 MOV Sreg: a data segment of DPL 3 is loadable at CPL 3 with RPL 3

undecided.why: the ring-3 code descriptor's readable bit is not stated in a pinned source, so whether es/ds/fs/gs may load it is undecided

null_seg_access.faults: an instruction with a memory operand whose segment register (default or by prefix) holds the null selector; lea, and a prefixed instruction without a memory operand, do not fault
null_seg_access.source: Intel SDM Vol 3 3.4.2 (a memory reference through a segment register that holds the null selector is #GP(0) at that instruction); Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: segv_handler TRAP_x86_PROTFLT lines 1925-1941 (err == 0 runs is_privileged_instr first, lines 1214-1271: prefixes skipped, 15 prefixes give EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION, then the opcode set above gives EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION; otherwise EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION, NumberParameters 2, ExceptionInformation[0] = 0, [1] = 0xffffffff because err & 7 != 4); check_invalid_gs line 1288 returns FALSE at a valid code address; setup_exception_record line 1449: ExceptionAddress = EIP_sig, Eip not advanced; segv_handler line 1905: rec = { 0 } so ExceptionFlags 0. Precedence (2): MSDN and the WDK state nothing for this case

precedence: (1) documented Win32 for Windows 7 SP1 build 7601: MSDN and WDK 7.1
(2) Wine 9.0, only where it contradicts neither (1) nor the declared OS
(3) nothing else (ReactOS is not a source)

gs.applies_to: every ring-3 thread whose trap frame's SegCs is the record's cs selector (all guest threads); a user CONTEXT with another RPL-3 code selector would keep its own gs
gs.source: Windows 7 SP1 (build 7601.17514) x86 kernels ntkrnlpa.exe sha256 d44e8f8420ea5040, ntoskrnl.exe sha256 d74e389d1a3ed4c7, both agreeing; _KTRAP_FRAME.SegGs = 0x30, SegCs = 0x6c (public PDB, OMAP applied; equal to WDK 7.1 ks386.inc TsSegGs / TsSegCs); KeContextToKframes stores SegGs = 0 (`and [tf+SegGs], 0`) when the trap frame's SegCs equals the record's cs selector 0x1b, and copies CONTEXT.SegGs only otherwise; KiInitializeContextThread (the user-thread initialization) calls it on the ContextFrame != 0 path and stores nothing to SegGs afterwards; KiThreadStartup reaches the exit sequence `lea esp, [frame+SegGs]; pop gs; ... iretd`, so user code starts with the frame's SegGs; PspCreateUserContext stores the same constant selectors as the record (cs, ds, es, ss, fs) and SegGs = 0

ss.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): KGDT_R3_DATA = 0x20 (the ring-3 data segment) | RPL_MASK 3

tr.source: WDK 7.1.0 ks386.inc (headers/_ks386.inc_00858): KGDT_TSS (the task state segment selector)

tss_io_bitmap.source: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c @ c8373ee49fb6: is_privileged_instr returns EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION for every in/out/ins/outs form with no per-port test (the instruction set is L3b's sdm_priv_rows.tsv, iopl class, not restated here), i.e. a Win32 user process has no permitted port; the documentation names the TSS I/O map (WDK 7.1 ks386.inc TssIoMapBase = 0x66, PrIopmOffset = 0x6E) and the exception (MSDN EXCEPTION_PRIV_INSTRUCTION: an instruction not allowed in the current machine mode) but states no permitted port for a user process, so it does not contradict Wine (precedence 2); with IOPL 0 (row eflags) every such instruction at CPL 3 is #GP(0), delivered as that exception
